data.title: Workbench Kit
data.description:
The prototype of the Workbench Kit: a parser for a JavaScript subset, a typed IR, emitters, and the tooling around them, so that a workbench (a domain language, an IDE, an agent and a book) can be built from a few small generated files instead of being regenerated whole every time.

Proposal: project/2026-11-23-workbench-kit-proposal.md. Rulings: project/2026-11-23-delivery-decisions.md. Platform findings: project/2026-11-23-m0-platform-probe.md.

data.title: M1: Game slice
data.description:
Tests hypotheses H1 (runtime lambdas fit comfortably in the subset) and H10 (the IR earns its keep) on a real grammar: the DMG Workbench's. Each runtime lambda in a preset is parsed from String(fn), lowered to IR and emitted as JS, then swapped into the DMG runtime in place of the original closure. Seeded traces of the original and swapped runs are compared.

Plan and binding decisions: project/2026-11-23-m1-game-slice-plan.md.

data.title: Typed IR, DMG dialect description, and lowering
data.description:
Why: the IR is meant to be the single source of truth that every backend, check and view reads (proposal §5). In the DMG Workbench, nothing depends on its IR, and behavior lives in opaque closures (finding L4, confirmed in project/2026-11-23-dmg-workbench-read.md). This leaf makes runtime behavior into data.

What:
- kit/ir/: a small typed IR with a diffable JSON form. It has types, functions, kernels (a function plus the domain it runs over), effects recorded on statements, and spans on every node.
- A lowering pass from the parser's AST, which resolves names and types against a dialect description and emits diagnostics: undeclared free variable, unknown member, type mismatch, effect not allowed in this domain.
- A DMG dialect description written in the kit's terms. Its inputs: the types of `self` (attributes with their types, baked constants, built-ins `x y index world alive visible`), the `w` surface the presets use (`frame`, `param`, `rand`, `rng.pick`, `board.at`/`filter`, `pool`, `spawn`, `emit`, `sfx`, `toast`, `input.*`, `grid.step`), `at(c,r).text` printf, and `Math.*`. Read attribute types from the built spec; keep the description beside the oracle harness or in kit/dialects/dmg/.

Already decided: integer semantics must match the oracle. Coercion happens on store, and an assignment expression evaluates to the unwrapped value, so `--self.ttl` on a u8 holding 0 yields −1 while 255 is stored. How the IR represents that is this leaf's call. Write the choice into the plan doc. Predicate lambdas to declared query intrinsics are allowed when they are pure. Strings are runtime values in this grammar (sprite names, choice params, event names), and so are entity references that may be empty.

Open, agent's call: whether a reference interpreter over the IR earns a place in M1. The proposal (§12) wants one eventually, but here the DMG runtime is the oracle. Ask the user before widening the subset beyond the predicate case.

Strictly test-first.

Out of scope: the emitter; GLSL, wasm and C.

Risk: return types like `"up" | {sprite, y} | null` and variadic printf may push the type system past what §5.2 lists. Record each such case for the H1 report rather than forcing it.

data.title: JavaScript emitter
data.description:
Why: the JS backend runs natively in the browser and is the code every other backend is compared against (proposal §6). Its output replaces the original closures in the differential run.

What: kit/emit/js/ turns an IR kernel into the source of a plain JS function with the same calling convention as the DMG slot it replaces: `(self, w)`, `(w, data)`, and so on. It carries the dialect's numeric rules and keeps a line map from emitted code back to source spans. Emitted code may call the DMG runtime's own `self`/`w` proxies; the point is to prove the lowering, not to replace the host.

Strictly test-first: unit tests per IR construct, then the emitted functions for presets 04–07, each checked against the oracle closure on recorded inputs where a whole-run trace would hide the cause.

Out of scope: other backends, optimization passes, and replacing the DMG runtime.

criteria.label: Every lowered lambda in presets 04–07 emits a function that the JS engine accepts (test).
Each emitted function maps every line back to its source span (test).
kit/emit/js/ imports no Node built-ins.

data.title: Differential run and H1/H10 report
data.description:
Why: this is M1's definition of done. It answers whether the approach works on a real grammar, and how comfortable the subset is, before any kit is extracted.

What:
- A script in scripts/ that, for presets 04–07, swaps every lowerable lambda for its emitted version and compares traces against the original. Use several seeds and generated input traces, over enough frames to reach game over where a game has one.
- The same script runs the lowering-only survey over all 22 presets: per preset, lambdas lowered, rejected with each reason, and the rewrites that would make each rejection lower.
- A dated findings doc in project/ that gives the verdict on H1 and H10, the subset widenings the evidence supports, and what M2 and M3 should change. Every figure names the command that reproduces it.
- The same doc corrects, in place, the proposal's errors listed in project/2026-11-23-dmg-workbench-read.md, each as a marked block quote. These are L5's overstated C coverage, L11's `lab:` links, L2's "mutation mode", the preset ids, and §5.8's wrap-before-compare.

Out of scope: fixing rejected presets by changing the DMG grammar.

criteria.label: For presets 04–07, every swapped run matches the original trace across the chosen seeds and input traces, or each mismatch is explained in the findings doc (script output).
The findings doc gives lowered/rejected counts for all 22 presets with reasons, and the command that reproduces them.
The proposal's factual errors are corrected in place as marked block quotes.

data.title: Oracle review fixes: trace coverage, bot input, test pinning
data.description:
Why: an independent review of b4f3b83 found that the oracle's traces miss differences a swapped lambda can cause, so a "match" in the M1 differential run would prove less than it claims. All findings were confirmed by red probes in the session scratchpad (review-oracle/gaps.test.mjs, P1–P8; mutate.sh for the test-pinning gap).

What (one surface: scripts/dmg-oracle/, tsconfig.json):
- S1: runTrace never calls rt.botInput(), so bot lambdas (presets 13, 20–24) never run and swapping one always matches. Add a way to drive input from the bot.
- M1: renderEvery defaults to 0, so draw/hud swaps (10 of 25 lambdas in presets 04–07) go undetected by default. Make the default exercise render.
- M2: TraceOptions.params throws (the DMG Runtime constructor calls set() before this.log exists). Make it work or remove it.
- M3: 16 of 22 single-line mutations leave the oracle suite green: trace fields (entity v, x/y, visible, alive, bg hash, bg scroll, oamStart, over/reason, fb hash, log data), rt.err ignored, firstDifference over min(len) ticks, no-op swaps for addRecord slots (methods, draw, done, bot) and for `every`, bot/inits omitted from lambdaSlots. Add a "changing X changes the trace" test per field and a swap test per slot kind.
- M4: 10 of 126 inventory lambdas reference top-level helpers/constants (DIRS, placeFood, scramble, …); the inventory doesn't flag this, so parse coverage is overstated. Flag it in the inventory and README.
- M5: skipLibCheck: true disables type-checking of the project's own .d.ts files.
- Minor: RNG draws not recorded (m1); bg hash covers tile indices, not glyph meaning (m2); snapshot of an event payload holding an entity proxy throws (m3); JSON snapshots merge NaN/null, undefined/absent, -0/0 (m4); timer `after` lambdas not listed or swappable (m5); firstDifference names `frame` instead of `error` on an erroring tick (m6).

data.title: Parser review fixes: spans, over-acceptance, fixits
data.description:
Why: an independent review of 9da34d4 found the parser builds wrong spans and accepts input JavaScript rejects or reads differently, and some fixits change meaning. Lowering and the emitter's line map trust this tree, so it is fixed before KHQFvD builds on it. Red probes: session scratchpad review-parser/probes.test.js (F1–F22, F12b, F16b; all 24 fail today), spans-corpus.mjs (23 of 3456 corpus expression spans don't compile alone), table.mjs, mutate.sh (18 of 21 mutants survive the suite).

Serious:
- S1: a node whose first operand is parenthesized starts its span inside the paren (parser.js:85-88, 283). Breaks the S104 fixit too.
- S2: the S104 template fixit doesn't parenthesize its concatenation: `a${b}`.length → "a" + (b).length.
- S3: `in` on plain objects (parser.js:123, 256; statements.js:30) makes valueOf/toString/constructor wrong nodes.

Moderate: M1 parseLambda throws (constructor outside try; RangeError on \u{110000}); M2 `??` mixed with ||/&& accepted; M3 legacy octal 010, "\1" mis-valued; M4 malformed numbers (1_, 0x, 1e) accepted, some as NaN; M5 reserved words as names; M6 parenthesized patterns and shorthand initializers outside patterns; M7 var→let fixit changes meaning under hoisting; M8 ==→=== fixit changes meaning; M9 S104 fixit mishandles CRLF and line continuations in templates.

Minor: N1 unicode identifier classes and line terminators (U+2028/9, lone CR); N2 newline before =>; N3 arrow as binary operand or callee; N4 assignment through an optional chain; N5 const without init, lexical decl as if body, for-of initializers, duplicate params/let; N6 HTML-like comments; N7 S116 fixit edits a comment; N8 TemplateElement ranges include delimiters; N9 over-strict P001s (trailing param comma, for(x in o), async(1)).

Rulings with Ben (2026-11-23): S116 keeps its warning and tip but loses its fixit. S112, S113, S114 are recorded as rejected in the plan's Parser rulings. M7: pending Ben's answer.

data.text:
IR leaf findings (irwright, 2026-11-23).

All 25 runtime lambdas in presets 04–07 lower to kernels with no diagnostics (scripts/dmg-lower/test/lower-corpus.test.js). An ad-hoc run of lowerPreset over all 22 presets lowered 104 of 126 (not a committed script; K4kgqD owns the survey).

Types past proposal §5.2, recorded for the H1 report (each was added rather than forced):
- str and string enums: sprite names, choice params, buttons, event and pool names. A string literal is a one-value enum; `"sweep"` vs choice `order` is checked against its options.
- Optional (possibly-empty) references: w.rng.pick, w.spawn, list.find. Lowering requires a check before use (narrowing on if (m), if (!m) return, m && …; const locals only), else L008.
- Union: the draw result, sprite-name | {sprite?, x?, y?, flipX?, flipY?} | null (presets 04–06); bot results; printf arguments (f64 | str | bool).
- Variadic printf: Cell.text(fmt: str, ...rest). The format string is not checked against the argument count.
- Lists with a maximum length (board 9, pool 24), so `each` loops are bounded; a list may carry extra members (the board's throwing `at`).
- Struct payloads and method signatures are inferred program-wide (DMG events and method params are untyped): payload from emit sites, params from call sites, result and effects from the method body, iterated to a fixed point.
- Keyed functions: w.param("x"), w.spawn("pool"), w.pool, w.sfx, w.all, w.one; the literal key selects the signature (L011 otherwise).

Reference interpreter: not in M1. The DMG runtime running the original closure is the oracle for every lambda, so an interpreter would be a third implementation checked against the same oracle and would test nothing H1 or H10 asks. It earns its place when a backend has no closure to compare with (GLSL in M2, or D1 operators); then it should be written against these IR goldens.

Gaps the 22-preset survey will show as rejections that are the lowering's, not the subset's: destructuring, for…of, array literals, `let x;`, `??`, reduce without an initial value (13 bot), string methods (.repeat 11, .toUpperCase 30) as L002, w.bg (21, 22, 26) not in the dialect, writes to w.oamStart (24, 30: the host's rule is (v|0)&255, not a declared store type) as L013, baked arrays/objects left out of the dialect.

JS emitter findings (irwright, 2026-11-23).

kit/emit/js emits every one of the 25 lowered lambdas in presets 04–07; each instantiates, and swapped alone into a fresh build, matches the original trace over 600 frames (seed 7, inputTrace(7, 600), renderEvery 4). Command: node --test scripts/dmg-lower/test/emit-oracle.test.js (about 1.2 s).

Numeric rules: values are JS doubles; a store is a plain assignment through the DMG proxy, which applies the attribute's coercion and logs its warnings (the trace compares those logs, so coercing in emitted code too would be wrong only in the logs, never silently). Recorded in the plan doc, "Integer semantics in the IR".

Sensitivity probe (ad hoc, not committed): mutating each emitted lambda (=== to !==, + to -, > to >=, return to return void, ! to !!) and re-running the same check caught 26 of 32 mutants. The 6 missed: > to >= on Mole.draw (05), Countdown.onFrame (06) and Spark.onFrame (07), whose boundary values never occur in 600 frames; return null to return undefined in 05 Mole.draw and return false to undefined in 06 whack, both equivalent to the host; and 06 done, which first fires at frame 2400. For K4kgqD: run long enough to reach game over, with several seeds.

data.title: IR review fixes: receiver evaluation, order, loop bounds, codes
data.description:
Why: an independent review of f8f6d3d found that compound assignment and ++/-- evaluate a non-stable receiver twice (duplicating RNG draws), plus ordering, loop-bound, reason-code and IR-spec gaps, and 13 of 24 semantic mutants that survive the suite. None of the 22 presets hits S1 today, but the IR's guarantees (left-to-right evaluation, bounded loops) must hold before the differential report leans on them. Probes: session scratchpad review-ir/ (h.js helper; p1, p2, p6, p7, p8, p10, p11, p12 are the reproductions).

Serious:
- S1: assign.js:28, 59-62, 102-104 re-evaluate the receiver for compound assignment and ++/--: `w.board.at(w.rng.int(9)).ttl += 30` emits two RNG draws (p1, p10).
Moderate:
- M1: compound assignment reads its target after the right side's spilled statements (assign.js:50, 62): `self.ttl += (self.ttl = 5)` gives 8 vs 10 (p2).
- M2: L007 checks only the test's shape; `for (let i = -1e17; i < 4; i++)` lowers and never ends (stmt.js:150-176, p7).
- M3: semantic tests are thin: 13 of 24 one-line mutants survive (p8); the find test (emit.test.js:77-83) passes for the wrong reason; empty-list some/every untested.
- M4: list indexing is reported as L009 but documented as L012 (expr.js:150, call.js:37); w.oamStart / w.over writes are rejected as L013 though the runtime's world set trap accepts them (dialects/dmg/index.js:96-97), presets 24 and 30.
- M5: `present` is used for any optional (f64?, bool?) but specified as "tests an optional"; it means JS truthiness (ir.d.ts:86, expr.js:312, p11).
Minor: m1 reduce evaluates init before its list (query.js:40,71); m2 a callback assigning an enclosing let gets no L006; m3 L004 bypassed via a method that fails to lower (failed() gives effects: []) and self-recursive methods; m4 browser-safe test misses `import "node:fs"`, dynamic import, `from"x"`, and relative imports leaving kit/ (p12); m5 ir.d.ts:35 and the plan say clamp-truncate-wrap but the host truncates then clamps (Runtime.prototype.coerce ~line 1216); m6 line map tested only for bounds; m7 `return w.end("crash")` in onFrame rejected as L003.

criteria.label: Every reproduction in review-ir/ (p1, p2, p6, p7, p11, p12) behaves correctly as a repo test
Each surviving mutant in review-ir/p8-mutants.mjs is killed, or its survival is explained
Reason codes and docs match: L009/L012 for indexing, world writes, present, coercion order

data.text:
irfix, D8Sv9n findings (2026-11-23), worktree agent-acb91cd0edae15b15.

Fixed, each with a red test first (kit/emit/js/test/semantics.test.js, kit/lower/test/review.test.js):

- S1/M1: placeFor({ once }) saves a non-stable receiver to a temp for compound assignment and ++/--; compound assignment now reads the target via seq([load, rhs]) so the old value is saved before a spilling right side (locals too: `a += (a = 5)` gives 6).
- m1: reduce saves a non-stable list to a temp when its init is also non-stable, so the list is evaluated first.
- M2: L007 unless the counter starts at a safe-integer literal (negation allowed) or w.param(...), and a constant bound is within 2^53. All presets' loops still lower (`dy = -1` included).
- M4: `list[i]` is L012 ("Indexing a list is not lowered yet"), any other computed name L009; README and code agree. w.oamStart (store u8) and w.over (store bool) are writable, read effects renamed `read World.over` / `read World.oamStart`. Preset 24's lambda now lowers: 105 of 126 lower, 21 rejected; all 105 match the original swapped alone on seeds 7 and 11 at 1200 frames (reviewer's p5 pointed at the worktree).
- M5: `present` only for opt of an entity ref (or union of refs); everything else is `truthy`. ir.d.ts says so.
- m2: assigning or updating any local inside a query callback is L006.
- m3: method sigs carry `calls` and `partial` (it or a callee failed). A draw/hud/every/after or a callback calling a partial method gets L014; a method on a call cycle gets L007 at the call.
- m4: browser-safe test rewritten around problems(text, file): bare import, `from"x"`, dynamic import(), require, and relative imports that leave kit/; JSDoc comments stripped first. Probe p12's strings are its own test.
- m5: ir.d.ts and the plan corrected (truncate, clamp, wrap) with a marked block quote.
- m6: line map test now checks statement spans exactly (kills mutant S).
- m7: `return f()` in a void slot lowers to do + return when f() is void.

Mutants (review-ir/p8-mutants.mjs, re-run on a copy of the worktree): all 24 killed or, for W, the pattern no longer exists (assign.js was rewritten); its replacements W2 (member) and W3 (local) are both killed, as are 9 new mutants of the fixes (Z1-Z9).

irfix, K4kgqD findings (2026-11-23), worktree agent-acb91cd0edae15b15. Report: project/2026-11-23-m1-findings.md; tool: scripts/dmg-diff/ (survey, diff, mutants verbs).

- Differential: `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js diff` — 10 cases over 04-07 (params: 04 sweep, 04 spawn 150 + sound off, 05 linger override 2.5, 07 burst/gravity extremes; plus "04 linger 0 (edited)", a derived program that makes the u16 wrap reachable) x seeds 7, 11, 23 x 3000 frames, each lambda alone and all at once: 30 runs, 0 differences. 06 done fires on every seed (over 601/156/601 ticks). Prerelease suite: scripts/dmg-diff/prerelease/diff.prerelease.js, 34 s.
- The shipped 04's wrap path is unreachable: linger's slider clamps overrides to 0.5, so ttl >= 30.
- Mutants: `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js mutants` — 9 p13 mutants: 5 caught, 4 equivalent under the host (reasons in sensitivity.js). y > 144 vs >= caught only by burst 6 on 2 of 3 seeds.
- Survey: `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js survey` — 126 lambdas: 105 lowered, 11 helpers (= inventory topLevelRefs), 9 not-yet (L012/L002/L015-on-reduce), 1 subset (23 bot, L007 step 8). Preset 02 has no runtime lambdas. Pinned in scripts/dmg-diff/test/dmg-diff.test.js.
- Proposal corrected in place (L2, L5, L11, §5.8 + preset 10 u16, preset ids under the roadmap); the DMG read's coercion order also corrected.
- Verdicts: H1 yes for the simpler half, open for the games (20-26: 14 of 21 rejections); H10 supported narrowly (closures removed for 04-07 headless; IR answered effects/order/bounds/store questions; one level falls short on coercion, inlined queries, present/truthy). Who owns passes: evidence leans to the passes note's middle path; left for Ben.

data.title: dmg-diff review fixes: guard the swap path, early stops, classifier gaps
data.description:
Why: an independent review of scripts/dmg-diff (35c4547) found nothing that undoes M1's figures, but the path that produces the headline number is unguarded. Probes were in the session scratchpad review-diff/ (may be gone; the reproductions are restated here).

1. No test checks that runCase actually swaps: changing differential.js:119 to swap into a fresh build nobody runs (`swapLambda(make().spec, s.id, s.fn)`) leaves npm test and the prerelease suite green. The smoke test counts emitted functions, not swaps. Red test: plant a fault through runCase (an emit hook or one MUTANTS entry) and expect a mismatch for that slot and for `*`.
3. A run that stops early on a runtime error reports a clean match: DiffResult records neither ticks run nor the error, and the CLI prints the requested frame count (differential.js:114-130, cli.js:59). Record ticks run and errors; fail when a run stops short.
4. 9 of the 30 runs are repeats (04 sweep, 05 default, 05 linger 2.5 are seed-independent): report distinct runs (24) or vary input/seed meaningfully; "ten param settings" includes 3 defaults and 1 edited program.
5. `mutants --json` always exits 0 (cli.js:72) against README line 12; an "equivalent" mutant that some run catches prints "caught" without flagging the wrong equivalence claim (cli.js:75,79).
6. 07 break->continue equivalence reason is wrong: a full-pool w.spawn logs "pool 'sparks' is full" once (seed 7: 998 failed spawns, 1 warning); fix the reason in sensitivity.js.
7. Survey classifier: kit/lower/stmt.js:40-42 doesn't lower a for...of body, hiding errors in it (23 Bird.onFrame hides an L002 for w.bg); survey.js:25 counts every L002 (typos too) as not-yet; survey.js:47 counts arity errors on filter/find/some/every as not-yet though its comment says reduce only.
8. Latent: runCase (differential.js:111) and probe (sensitivity.js:51) swap only the first part's emitted function for a fragment lambda used by several parts; no preset has one today.
9. "Each of the 105 lowered lambdas, swapped in alone, matches on seeds 7 and 11 over 1200 frames" has no committed command; add one (e.g. a `diff --all-presets` verb in the prerelease suite, ~15 s).

data.title: Lower the ruled subset widenings: helpers, for…of, destructuring, indexing
data.description:
Why: Ben ruled on M1's subset widenings (project/2026-11-23-m1-game-slice-plan.md, "Subset widenings after M1"). Lowering them turns most of M1's 21 rejections into lowered lambdas, and the differential run then checks them.

What (strictly test-first; each item red first):
- Lower top-level program helpers as program functions, like DMG methods. Top-level constants become baked constants. Check whether the 6 presets' helpers are arrows or `function` declarations; a top-level function declaration may need a parser change.
- Lower `for…of` over a bounded list, and struct destructuring. Fix lowering skipping a `for…of` body (dmg-diff review finding 7, kit/lower/stmt.js:40-42).
- Lower list indexing, typed as possibly empty, and tuple destructuring.
- Improve L007's tip for a non-unit step: suggest the counted rewrite.
- Re-run the survey and the differential run, extending the prerelease suite to the newly lowered lambdas, and record the new counts as a marked update to the M1 findings.

data.title: Rule on the next H1 gates: array literals, w.bg, call-site type joins
data.description:
Why: after the widenings (96954db), 2 of 11 helper lambdas lower, not the ~7 expected. The remaining gates on H1 for the games are mostly two things, plus one inference limit. Each needs a ruling from Ben before it is built.

1. Array literals are not lowered. They block 20 Ball ([w.player, w.cpu]), 21 snake and its DIRS constant, 23 Bird ([[3,2],…]) and 25 at16. Tuple destructuring has nothing to destructure until they lower. The fork: type a literal as {list: T, max: n}, so each item is possibly empty (consistent with indexing), or add a fixed-length tuple type whose items are non-empty (more precise, and a new type in the core IR).
2. w.bg is not in the DMG dialect. It blocks 21 placeFood, 22 breakout.on(brick), 23 Bird, 25 flip, 26 Cursor, and probably 26 step. Describing it means typing the background API (cell reads and writes, scroll) and its effects. This is dialect work, not subset work.
3. Call-site typing for methods and helpers is first-wins. Two call sites that pass different string literals (enum types) mismatch at the second. Joining types across call sites would fix this for both.
Minor: a helper whose only callers fail to lower gets no call sites, so L014 says its parameters cannot be inferred. This is correct but noisy (writeCol).
Source: the m82n5e agent's report; counts from `node scripts/dmg-diff/cli.js survey`.
